stemMd: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 13 cm and base 10 cm. What is its height to the base?
explanationMd: The altitude bisects the base into two five-centimetre segments. Each right triangle has hypotenuse thirteen, so height is √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.

distractorRationale.a: This does not satisfy the right triangle formed by the altitude.
distractorRationale.d: This uses the full base rather than half the base in Pythagoras.
distractorRationale.c: This is the sloping side, not the altitude.
